watches.name: 125 Field | Australian Army 125th Anniversary
watches.description: Officially authorised by the Australian Army. Limited to 125 individually numbered pieces. Built to mark 125 years of the Australian Army, 1901 to 2026. A field watch made for the people who serve, and made with them. Produced under formal authorisation from the Australian Army to reproduce the Rising Sun 8th Pattern emblem, dated 18 August 2026. Each watch is engraved 001/125 through 125/125. That is the entire run. Included in the box: Brushed 316L stainless steel oyster bracelet Parachute-style elastic olive NATO strap Quick-release spring bars for tool-free strap changes Made to order. 10-week production once your order is confirmed. Free worldwide shipping. AUD $50 from every watch goes to an Australian veterans' welfare charity. This watch started with the people who would wear it. It began with a single social media post. More than 400 serving members, veterans and supporters of the Australian Army put their hands up and said they wanted it built. That is the number that started this. Not a marketing plan, a show of hands. So we opened the design to them. Nine months of community input shaped the dial, the straps, the engraving and the charity that receives the contribution. Then every detail went to the Australian Army for approval. “We didn't build a watch and put an Army badge on it. We asked the people who'd wear it what it should be, we listened to their answers, and we submitted every detail to the Australian Army for approval. Every choice on this watch was earned.” — Christophe Hoppé, founder A tribute to the 1944 W.W.W. specification The 125 Field takes its design language from the 1944 W.W.W. specification, Watch, Wristlet, Waterproof. That was the British Ministry of Defence brief that defined the modern military field watch, and produced the twelve Swiss-built watches now known as the Dirty Dozen. Matte black dial. Cream lume numerals in period-correct typography. Sword hands. Small seconds. The 125 Field carries that lineage forward, with one addition, a small red kangaroo above centre. A discreet Australian marker on an otherwise universal soldier's watch. This is a tribute to the W.W.W. spec. It is not a claim of Australian-issue lineage. There is no documented record of W.W.W. watches being officially issued to the Australian Army. The broad arrow, restored to service. The broad arrow was struck onto British and Commonwealth military-issue equipment. Rifles, watches, kit, everything owned by the Crown. On the 125 Field it is raised and stamped on the top of the crown, where you see it on the wrist. The same mark that appeared on the original 1944 W.W.W. watches, restored to service on a watch built for the modern Australian soldier. The watch The dial Matte black with a fine sandy grain, made to catch light the way ground does in a low afternoon sun. Cream Super-LumiNova numerals in Old Radium tone, painted to match the warmth of aged tritium, set in period-correct field typography. A sunken small-seconds sub-dial at 4:30, marked “125 ARMY” in signal red. A small red kangaroo above centre. White printing on the chapter ring, kept minimal. The hands Bead-blasted silver hour and minute hands, filled with Old Radium luminous. A flat sword profile, the kind of hand that disappears in daylight and reappears the moment the light goes. The seconds sit in the offset sub-dial, bead-blast silver, no decoration. The case 316L stainless steel, 38mm wide, 46mm lug to lug, around 11mm thick. Brushed finish, matte, hard-wearing, no glare, no jewellery polish. Domed sapphire crystal with internal anti-reflective treatment. Drilled lugs. 10 ATM water resistance. A Miyota 82S5 Japanese automatic sits inside. Sub-seconds, hacking, hand-winding, 21,600 vph, around 42 hours of power reserve. Chosen for reliability under field conditions and ease of long-term service. The crown Oversized and knurled, 316L, screw-down, with the broad arrow raised and stamped on top. Inside the crown chamber, Australian earth taken from a site

watches.name: City Lights
watches.description: Friday night. You don't leave the city, you let it switch on around you. The lights come up, the night opens, and there's nowhere else you'd rather be. Paddington. A Melbourne laneway. James Street. Elizabeth Quay. Pick your version, a rooftop over the harbour, a table that runs past midnight, the good end of town after dark. TThat's the colour this dial carries. Black, with a hint of violet, the colour a city sky never quite lets go of. The good life, lit up. Rated to 200 metres. Inside the crown, a piece of the Australian coast.

specsRaw.Outer ring: brushed steel, 60-minute dive scale. Inner ring: polished, 12-hour scale to track a second timezone. One uni-directional action, two distinct finishes.

watches.name: Long Weekend
watches.description: Friday afternoon. The city drops away behind you, the road opens, and the weekend starts before you've even arrived. Noosa, Mornington Peninsula, and Palm Beach / Southern Highlands... pick your version. Salt air or red dust, a long lunch that runs into the evening, nowhere you have to be. Th at's the colour this dial carries. Warm, sun-bleached, easy. The good life, wide open. Rated to 200 metres. Inside the crown, a piece of the Australian coast.

watches.name: Royal Australian Engineers 125th Anniversary watch
watches.description: Royal Australian Engineers 125th Anniversary — the first 125 pieces are a numbered limited edition. Designed with the Royal Australian Engineers to mark 125 years of service. A field watch built on the same principles the Corps was built on — make what's needed, hold what's given, finish what's started. The first 125 pieces are individually engraved 001/125 through 125/125. After that, the watch continues — without the numbering. Be first to secure a piece of limited edition history. Included in the box: 316L stainless steel oyster bracelet Maroon & navy parachute strap (RAE Corps colours) Quick-release spring bars for tool-free strap changes Made to order. 10-week production once your order is confirmed. Free worldwide shipping. AUD $75 from every watch goes to the RAE Foundation. This watch started at Holsworthy. In May 2026, I drove out to Holsworthy Barracks — home of the Royal Australian Engineers and the Corps museum. I wanted to see what 125 years of Engineers actually looked like before I put a single line on a design page. We spent the day going through the museum. The tools the Corps has used since 1902 — bridging equipment, demolition kits, field instruments, the small everyday things sappers carry. The photographs. The names on the walls. You can read the history. It's another thing to stand in front of it. That's the visit that gave the watch its shape. The grainy black dial — the texture of sandy ground under a field engineer's boot. The applied numerals with Old Radium lume — readable in the dark, the way a field watch has to be. The bead-blasted case — no shine, no glare, no jewellery polish. The maroon and navy parachute strap — the Corps colours, woven into something you can wear every day. Then came the back-and-forth. Sketches. Revisions. Thomas and the committee asking for changes that mattered — proportions, the dial layout, the weight of the motto on the caseback, where the lazy E sat on the crown. We iterated for months. What you see is what we agreed on, together. The watch The dial A grainy "sandy" black dial — textured to catch light the way ground does in a low afternoon sun. Applied numerals in Old Radium luminous, painted to match the warmth of aged tritium without the regulation. A sunken sub-second at 6 o'clock. White printing on the chapter ring for legibility, kept minimal. The dial reads "bausele / RAE" — nothing more. The hands Bead-blasted silver hour and minute hands, filled with SL-Old Radium luminous. The shape is a flat sword profile — the kind of hand that disappears in daylight and reappears the moment the light goes. The seconds hand sits in the sub-dial at 6 — finished in bead-blast silver, no contrast colour, no decoration. The case 316L stainless steel, 38mm wide, 46mm lug-to-lug. Fully bead-blasted with an anti-fingerprint coating — matte, hard-wearing, no reflection to give away position. Box sapphire crystal with internal anti-reflective treatment. 7mm screw-down crown in the same bead-blast finish, engraved with the Corps' lazy E. 10 ATM water resistance. A Miyota 82S5 automatic movement sits inside — chosen for reliability under field conditions and ease of long-term service. UBIQUE — Facimus et Frangimus "Everywhere — We Make and We Break" The caseback carries the Royal Australian Engineers' regimental crest and motto, engraved into a screw-down 316L back. UBIQUE — "Everywhere." Granted to the Corps for serving in every theatre the Australian Army has been deployed to since federation. FACIMUS ET FRANGIMUS — "We make and we break." The full sentence of the sapper's trade: the Engineers build what's needed and destroy what blocks the way. The first 125 watches are individually engraved with their edition number — 001/125 through 125/125 — and the inscription "ROYAL AUSTRALIAN ENGINEERS · 125th Anniversary." Beyond 125, the inscription remains but the individual numbering ends. Two straps, both in the box Oyster link bracelet 316L stainless steel, 18×16mm oyster-link construct

watches.name: Elemental Bathurst Limited Edition
watches.description: Mount Panorama. 6.2 kilometres of bitumen that breaks cars and builds legends. The rubber that gets laid into that circuit during the 12 Hour doesn't just wear off, it gets claimed by it. That's what's sealed in the crown. Limited to 50 pieces. Sold at the circuit. Gone before the chequered flag. The crown chamber holds tyre rubber from a race car that competed at Bathurst. Movement: Swiss Sellita SW200 automatic — 4 Hz, 38-hour power reserve, Special grade.

watches.name: AIR FORCE 5th GENERATION
watches.description: Bausele Air Force 5th Generation. The official watch of the Royal Australian Air Force, honouring a legacy of service, precision and national pride. Built around a 42mm brushed stainless steel case and powered by the trusty Swiss Sellita SW200 automatic movement, the Air Force 5th Generation is engineered for serving members and aviation enthusiasts who demand both heritage and capability. The deep blue sunray dial features Super-LumiNova® BGW9 hands and indices for unparalleled night-time visibility, while the screw-down crown holds soil from RAAF Base Point Cook — Australia's oldest military air base, in operation since 1914. Rated to 200 metres of water resistance and protected by scratch-resistant sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating, this is a tool watch built for those who serve. Limited to 200 individually numbered pieces. Designed in Australia. Powered by Swiss precision.
